title: Miso Soup with Tofu
description: A proper dashi made from kombu and bonito, with soft cubes of silken tofu, wakame and white miso whisked in off the heat. Quiet, savoury and far better than anything from a sachet.

steps.text: Put the kombu and cold water in a saucepan and leave to soak. This is where most of the flavour is drawn out, and it needs no attention.
steps.tip: Do not wash off the white bloom on the kombu — it is full of savoury flavour. A wipe with a damp cloth is enough.

steps.text: Set the pan over a low heat and bring it slowly up to the point where small bubbles gather at the edge, taking about 10 minutes. Lift out the kombu just before it boils.
Bring the liquid to a simmer, scatter in the bonito flakes and turn off the heat. Leave them to steep and sink.

Meanwhile, cover the wakame with cold water in a small bowl and leave to swell for 5 minutes, then drain. Strain the dashi through a fine sieve into a jug, pressing lightly on the flakes, and return it to the rinsed pan.
Warm the dashi over a low heat until steaming. Add the tofu and wakame and heat gently for 2 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat. Put the miso in a ladle or small bowl, whisk in a little of the hot dashi until smooth, then stir it into the soup. Taste and add a touch more miso if you like.
steps.tip: Never boil the soup once the miso is in. It dulls the aroma and makes the texture grainy.

steps.text: Ladle into small bowls, dividing the tofu evenly, and scatter with the spring onions. Serve straight away.

tips: Stir the soup just before each sip. Miso settles naturally.
Miso varies a great deal in saltiness, so start with 3 tbsp if yours is a darker type.

substitutions.use: 3 dried shiitake mushrooms soaked with the kombu
1 litre water with 2 tsp instant dashi powder

storage: Best eaten as soon as it is made. The dashi alone keeps for 3 days in the fridge; add miso and tofu when you reheat it.
author: Simmer
